input:
/data/legacy holds text files in mixed encodings. For every file whose name ends in `.txt` (case-sensitive), write a normalised copy with the same name to /out/clean/: UTF-8 without BOM, line endings 
 and lone  converted to 
, and ending with exactly one added 
 if the text did not already end with 
.
Detect each file's encoding in this order: starts with a UTF-16 BOM (FF FE or FE FF) -> utf-16; starts with the UTF-8 BOM -> utf-8-sig; decodes as UTF-8 -> utf-8 (plain ASCII included); otherwise latin-1.
Write /out/manifest.tsv (tab-separated, header name, encoding, lines, chars) with one row per file sorted by name, where lines is the number of 
 and chars the number of Unicode characters in the normalised text (newlines included, BOM excluded).

transcript.final_response:
I wrote normalised copies of the six `.txt` files to `/out/clean/` and the manifest to `/out/manifest.tsv`. `g.TXT` was skipped because its extension is uppercase and the match is case-sensitive.

| name | encoding | lines | chars |
|---|---|---|---|
| a.txt | utf-8 | 2 | 24 |
| b.txt | utf-8-sig | 2 | 26 |
| c.txt | latin-1 | 2 | 23 |
| d.txt | utf-16 | 3 | 16 |
| e.txt | utf-8 | 2 | 30 |
| f.txt | latin-1 | 3 | 17 |

I only spot-checked `a.txt`, whose raw bytes are valid UTF-8 and were detected as `utf-8`. I did not open the output files to check their contents.
tool_calls:
cd /data/legacy && cat > /tmp/r.py <<'E'
import os
src='/data/legacy'; out='/out/clean'
os.makedirs(out,exist_ok=True)
rows=[]
for n in sorted(os.listdir(src)):
    p=os.path.join(src,n)
    if not n.endswith('.txt') or not os.path.isfile(p): continue
    b=open(p,'rb').read()
    if b[:2] in (b'\xff\xfe',b'\xfe\xff'): enc='utf-16'
    elif b[:3]==b'\xef\xbb\xbf': enc='utf-8-sig'
    else:
        try: b.decode('utf-8'); enc='utf-8'
        except UnicodeDecodeError: enc='latin-1'
    t=b.decode(enc).replace('\r\n','\n').replace('\r','\n')
    if not t.endswith('\n'): t+='\n'
    open(os.path.join(out,n),'wb').write(t.encode('utf-8'))
    rows.append((n,enc,t.count('\n'),len(t)))
with open('/out/manifest.tsv','w',encoding='utf-8',newline='') as f:
    f.write('name\tencoding\tlines\tchars\n')
    for r in rows: f.write('\t'.join(map(str,r))+'\n')
E
python3 /tmp/r.py; cat /out/manifest.tsv; xxd a.txt | head -3
